subject: Evotech POC: acceptance gates, perf targets, and ops cadence
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Cole <avery@evotech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Evotech POC: acceptance gates, perf targets, and ops cadence

Hi Avery / Samir —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC timeline and responsibilities. I focused the success criteria on the three things we discussed: latency, throughput/capacity, and cost with a lightweight quality check. Please confirm or call out any changes.

1) Acceptance gates (what indicates POC success)
  - Latency: 95th percentile tail (p95) for representative traffic <= 200 ms for median prompt length (40–80 tokens). We will also capture p50 and p99 for visibility.
  - Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec with 99% of requests served within the p95 latency target. Short bursts up to 250 rps acceptable for 5–10s.
  - Cost: measured cost/token for the trial traffic <= $0.0009/token (end-to-end: tokens consumed by model + inferred infra overhead).
  - Quality: automated metrics (BLEU / embedding similarity on labeled set) + human-review sample: target > 0.85 pass rate on the labeled 500-case set, and average human rating >= 4.0/5.

2) Test plan / how we measure
  - Data set: Evotech provides a 2k-sample prompt/response set (redacted) we will use for initial smoke and accuracy checks. (Attached: evotech-sample-prompts.csv)
  - Traffic: production-traffic replay from a 24h window to Redwood staging for latency/throughput tests. If replay not available, we will synthesize based on your traffic profile.
  - Environments: Redwood staging (shared) for initial validation; Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) for final acceptance run if you want production parity.
  - Measurement windows: 30-minute steady-state windows for throughput runs; multiple 5–10s burst tests for spiky scenarios.

3) Roles & owners
  - Customer lead: Avery / Samir (Evotech) — confirm sample dataset and access.
  - Sales / Program: Karthik (Redwood) — commercial & cadence.
  - CS onboarding & evaluation lead: Monica (Redwood) — quality checks, human evaluation.
  - SRE / performance: Ben (Redwood) — test harness, load profile, monitors.
  - Ops / provisioning: Priyom (Redwood) — Dedicated capacity and quota.

4) Timeline (proposal)
  - Sep 18 — 30min kickoff (confirm dataset + SOW scope)
  - Sep 20–24 — data handoff + smoke validation on staging
  - Sep 25–28 — throughput / latency runs (steady-state and burst)
  - Oct 1 — runbook + acceptance readout (pass/fail)

5) Commercial & trial mechanics
  - We can run a 30-day trial under a short SOW. Attached is a draft SOW for your review (redwood-trial-sow-draft.pdf). The SOW includes options for Hosted vs Dedicated capacity and an estimate model for cost/token given projected throughput.
  - If Dedicated is preferred we'll provision reserved GPUs for the acceptance window to mirror production.

Please confirm the acceptance gates above, the owners, and the proposed kickoff time (Sep 18 — I can do 10:00–11:30 PT). Also confirm whether Evotech will supply a redacted 2k prompt set or whether we should synthesize.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks Karthik — this is great and captures the main points. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering side:

- For latency targets: can you confirm whether the p95 target is measured at the Redwood edge (your API) or end-to-end including our network hop? Evotech would like to clearly separate network variance from model processing.
- For cost/token: we need the cost breakdown so our procurement folks can estimate. Is the $0.0009 figure pure model inference cost or does it include a margin for infra and SRE overhead?
- Quality: the 500-case human review sample is fine — can we align on the rubric (pass/fail categories) before Monica begins evaluations?

Security question: our security team will want a copy of your SOC2 report and confirmation about logs retention for trial (we prefer logs for 30 days). Who can I share a questionnaire with?

We will provide a redacted 2k prompt set by Sep 17 EOD. Kickoff on Sep 18 10:00 PT works for us.

—Avery
Avery Cole
Head of ML Platform, Evotech Labs
avery@evotech.com

For acceptance we recommend using Redwood "edge" numbers to keep the measurements deterministic; we’ll include your runner results in the readout packet.

- Cost breakdown: the $0.0009/token is an example blended figure. We'll produce a simple cost model that separates (i) model compute, (ii) GPU provisioning overhead (if Dedicated), (iii) network / caching overhead, and (iv) Redwood platform fees. That sheet will be included with the SOW draft.

- Quality rubric: Monica — can you draft a one-page rubric with pass/fail buckets and a 1–5 human rating scale? We can circulate for sign-off before human evals start.

- Security / SOC2: Monica will own the questionnaire intake and will share our SOC2 report & security packet. Monica — sending the security contact for Evotech would help (CC’d).

I’ll upload the trial SOW draft to DocuSign after we confirm kickoff. Link: https://docusign.net/EVT-2026-0042/SOW

See you on the 18th — Karthik
